intent: The first modern Olympic champion was not a Greek and not a runner: a Boston student who quit Harvard, crossed the Atlantic by cargo ship and won the triple jump on day one — shown as a jump against a bus and a drawn sea route.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Who won the FIRST gold medal of the modern Olympics?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Who won the first gold medal of the modern Olympics?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: The United States. James Connolly, a Boston student, won the triple jump in Athens on 6 April 1896.

lines.direction: tight on Athens; the compare blocks rise on 'hopped' — Connolly's jump beside a London bus — the medal sticker on 'metres', the bus sticker and a Greece dim-light on 'bus'
lines.text: He hopped, skipped and jumped nearly 14 metres, further than a London bus is long.

lines.direction: pull out to the whole Atlantic; Boston pin and tag on 'harvard'; the sad flag-ball on 'quit'; from 'ship' the freighter route draws east across the ocean to Athens with the ship sticker popping at Boston
lines.text: Harvard refused him leave to go, so he quit, and crossed the Atlantic by cargo ship to compete.

lines.direction: back in on Athens; the 1,500 YEARS card on 'crowned'; the laurel sticker on 'years'; the stadium pin pulses and the happy flag-ball pops on 'dropout'
lines.text: No Olympic champion had been crowned for 1,500 years, and the man who ended the wait was a dropout.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
